label: Kyiv
sub: Capital city; survived 2022 siege; sustained missile/drone strikes throughout war

label: Kharkiv
sub: Ukraine's 2nd city; survived 2022 capture attempt; near active frontline; under daily Russian shelling

label: Mariupol
sub: Besieged and occupied May 2022; Azovstal defenders' last stand; city largely destroyed

label: Bakhmut
sub: Site of war's longest, bloodiest battle (Aug 2022–May 2023); captured by Wagner Group

label: Avdiivka
sub: Ukrainian stronghold since 2014; fell to Russia Feb 18, 2024 — Russia's biggest gain of 2024

label: Kherson
sub: Regional capital; liberated Nov 11, 2022; still shelled from Russian positions across Dnipro

label: Zaporizhzhia
sub: Frontline regional center; under regular Russian missile and drone attacks

label: Zaporizhzhia NPP
sub: Europe's largest nuclear plant; Russian-occupied since Mar 4, 2022; 6 reactors shut down; IAEA mission ongoing. June 1, 2026 (IAEA Update 307): drone struck turbine hall exterior next to reactor unit 6 — first drone strike within ZNPP perimeter since April 2024. Radiation levels normal. IAEA DG Grossi: 'Attacks on nuclear sites are unacceptable.'

label: Odesa
sub: Key Black Sea port city; major Russian strike target; critical for Ukrainian grain exports; protected by air defense

label: Dnipro
sub: Major industrial city; key logistics hub; sustained major missile strikes including Jan 2023 apartment building attack

label: Kramatorsk
sub: Administrative center of Ukrainian-held Donetsk Oblast; regular Russian strike target; railroad hub

label: Izyum
sub: Key Russian logistics hub liberated Sep 2022 counteroffensive; mass graves found post-liberation

label: Melitopol
sub: Russian-controlled city; key hub on land corridor to Crimea; primary target of failed 2023 counteroffensive

label: Bucha
sub: Site of documented Russian war crimes; hundreds of civilian bodies found after Russian withdrawal Apr 2022

label: Soledar
sub: Salt-mining town captured by Wagner Jan 2023; precursor to Bakhmut fall

label: Kakhovka Dam
sub: Destroyed Jun 6, 2023; caused catastrophic flooding; 1M+ lost water access; Russia accused of sabotage

label: Kerch Bridge
sub: Partially destroyed by Ukraine Oct 8, 2022 and Oct 2023; key supply route to occupied Crimea

label: Sevastopol
sub: Russian Black Sea Fleet HQ in occupied Crimea; targeted by Ukrainian drone and missile strikes throughout war

label: Tokmak
sub: Key Russian logistics hub in occupied Zaporizhzhia; primary HIMARS strike target; goal of 2023 Ukrainian counteroffensive

label: Pokrovsk
sub: Critical Ukrainian logistics hub in Donetsk; under intense Russian pressure since 2024; key to Ukrainian supply lines

label: Lyman
sub: Railroad hub liberated by Ukraine in Sep 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive; key rail hub for Donbas

label: Lviv
sub: Key western logistics hub for NATO weapons deliveries; Polish border crossing point; major refugee transit city

label: Orikhiv
sub: Frontline town in Zaporizhzhia Oblast; focal point of 2023 Ukrainian counteroffensive breakthrough attempts

label: Dnipro River Line
sub: Active front along Dnipro River east of Kherson; Ukraine holds west bank; Russia east bank since Nov 2022

label: Chasiv Yar
sub: Key elevated position near Bakhmut; under intense Russian pressure since 2024; controls approaches to Kramatorsk

label: Mykolaiv
sub: Southern city; defended Ukrainian flank protecting Odesa; sustained Russian strikes throughout 2022

label: Sumy
sub: Border city; under frequent Russian cross-border shelling; Ukrainian forces used Sumy as staging for Kursk incursion

label: Donetsk City
sub: Russian-controlled administrative center of occupied Donetsk Oblast; occupied since 2014; front lines 10–15 km from city center

label: Kharkiv-Belgorod Front
sub: Active Russian cross-border pressure zone; Russia opened offensive from Belgorod into Kharkiv Oblast May 2024

label: Polish Border Crossing
sub: Primary NATO weapons and aid entry point into Ukraine; Medyka/Shehyni crossings handle bulk of military deliveries

label: Patriot Air Defense
sub: Patriot PAC-3 batteries positioned to defend Kyiv; successfully intercepted Kinzhal hypersonic missiles in May 2023

label: Snake Island
sub: Small island in Black Sea; captured by Russia Feb 2022; retaken by Ukraine Aug 7, 2022; site of famous Ukrainian defiance

label: Vuhledar
sub: Strategic mining town; Ukraine inflicted major Russian armored losses in early 2023; fell to Russia Oct 2024

label: Krasnohorivka
sub: Frontline town near Donetsk; contested throughout 2023–2024; Russia captured portions in 2024

label: Luhansk City
sub: Administrative center of Russian-occupied Luhansk Oblast; held by Russia since 2014

label: Kherson Oblast Front
sub: Southern front along Dnipro River; Ukraine holds Kherson city; Russia holds east bank including Oleshky

label: Kharkiv Aid Hub
sub: UNHCR and international NGO coordination hub for northeast Ukraine; critical humanitarian logistics center

label: Crimea Peninsula
sub: Russian-occupied since 2014; formally annexed; HQ of Black Sea Fleet; targeted by Ukrainian long-range strikes

label: Lipetsk Air Base (Russia)
sub: Russian air base targeted by Ukrainian long-range drones in 2024; housed Su-34 aircraft used for strikes

label: Sudzha (Russia – Kursk)
sub: Largest town captured by Ukraine in Aug 2024 Kursk incursion; recaptured by Russia Mar 2025

label: Izmail Port
sub: Danube river port; Russia attacked grain infrastructure here after withdrawing from Black Sea grain deal Jul 2023

label: Hulyaipole
sub: Ukrainian forces reported an advance in the Hulyaipole direction, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, on May 17, 2026. Russia has been pressing westward toward the provincial capital; Ukraine's tactical advance reversed gains. Active frontline zone with 23+ Russian assault attempts per day.

label: Sloviansk
sub: Northern anchor of Ukraine's 'Fortress Belt'; under Russian pressure since spring 2026 offensive; mandatory evacuations ordered Mar 2026

label: Kostiantynivka
sub: Southern anchor of 'Fortress Belt'; heavily contested in 2026 spring offensive; key Ukrainian defensive position in Donetsk Oblast

label: Poltava
sub: Regional center; energy infrastructure struck in Russia's March 24, 2026 mass missile attack causing regional power outages

label: Ilsky Refinery (Krasnodar)
sub: Russian oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai struck by Ukrainian drones March 27, 2026; second consecutive night of strikes on Russian energy in region

label: Odesa Maternity Hospital Strike
sub: Russia struck Odesa with 60+ drones on March 28, 2026, hitting a maternity hospital roof, 3 educational institutions, and apartment buildings; 2 killed, 11 injured; 81 evacuated

label: Kovsharovka (Captured)
sub: Captured by Russian 1st Guards Tank Army on March 29, 2026 — largest urbanized settlement (pop. ~17,960) seized in Kharkiv Oblast spring offensive; Russian forces pressing toward Kupyansk-Uzlovoi

label: Ozernoye Airbase (Zhytomyr)
sub: Ukrainian military airbase struck by at least 7 Russian Geran-2 kamikaze UAVs on March 29, 2026; base serves combined combat aviation and personnel training

label: Kryvyi Rih Industrial Strike
sub: Russian drone struck an industrial site in Kryvyi Rih on March 29, 2026, killing 1 man and igniting fires; part of 442-drone overnight barrage

label: Taganrog (Russia — Struck)
sub: Ukrainian drone strike killed 1 and wounded several in Taganrog, Rostov Oblast on March 31, 2026; dozens of residential buildings damaged; part of Ukraine's deep-strike campaign

label: Nikopol Drone Strike
sub: Russian drone strike on April 1, 2026 injured 11 people including a child in Nikopol, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast; infrastructure damage reported

label: Podoly (Russian Claim)
sub: Russian MoD claimed seizure of Podoly village near Kupyansk, Kharkiv Oblast on April 1, 2026; Ukrainian GS did not confirm; Russian forces pressing toward Kupyansk-Uzlovoi

label: Chuhuiv Strike (Apr 2)
sub: Russian drone struck a residential building in Chuhuiv, Kharkiv Oblast on April 2, 2026, igniting fires on two floors and injuring 3 women; part of continued Russian strikes on Kharkiv Oblast civilian infrastructure

label: Bryansk Missile Factory (UA Strike)
sub: Ukraine struck a manufacturing components facility for 'Strela' cruise missiles in Bryansk region on April 2, 2026; part of the ongoing deep-strike campaign against Russian defense-industrial infrastructure

label: Kirovske Airfield (UA Strike, Apr 3)
sub: Ukrainian military intelligence struck Kirovske military airfield in occupied Crimea overnight April 2–3, 2026; part of sustained campaign to degrade Russian air assets in the peninsula

label: Kharkiv Ballistic Strike (Apr 3)
sub: Russia fired 4 ballistic missiles at Kharkiv on April 3, 2026, striking residential buildings and igniting a fire in the Osnovianskyi district; 1 woman injured; Kharkiv has endured 20+ strikes in early April alone

label: Novorossiysk Energy Hub (UA Strike)
sub: Ukraine struck Russian Black Sea energy hub at Novorossiysk on April 6, 2026, expanding its deep-strike campaign against Russian energy infrastructure beyond oil refineries to Black Sea export terminals

label: Odesa Port Strike (Apr 8)
sub: Russian drone struck critical infrastructure at Odesa port on April 8, 2026, continuing Moscow's campaign to disrupt Ukraine's primary Black Sea maritime export hub

label: Belarus Border Road Construction (Apr 18)
sub: New road construction near the Belarus-Ukraine border raises fears of Belarusian re-entry into the conflict, mirroring logistics staging seen before the 2022 invasion.

label: Tuapse Oil Refinery (Struck)
sub: Ukraine struck Russia's Tuapse oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai twice in one week — April 16 ('volcano' fires) and April 20 (confirmed second strike, 1 killed). Refinery processes ~12 million tons of crude annually; part of Ukraine's sustained campaign against Russian energy export infrastructure.

label: Nizhyn (Chernihiv Oblast)
sub: Russian drone and rocket strikes on April 25, 2026 killed 2 people and injured 2 others. 27 attacks reported in the Nizhyn area in the preceding day. Part of Russia's mass 666-UAV/missile attack, one of the largest of the year.

label: Huliaipole (Zaporizhzhia)
sub: Active frontline sector in Zaporizhzhia Oblast under intensifying Russian pressure in April 2026. Russian forces advancing west of Gulyaypole; 18 combat engagements on April 26. Civilian minibus struck by guided aerial bomb, killing 1 and injuring 4.

label: Chornomorsk Port (Repeated Strikes)
sub: Russian drone strikes hit Chornomorsk repeatedly — April 27 caused a ~6,000-ton sunflower oil spill into the Black Sea; May 2-3 killed 2 people and damaged 35 homes. Key Ukrainian grain/commodity export hub 30 km SW of Odesa.

label: Merefa (Iskander-M)
sub: Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile struck Merefa, Kharkiv district on May 4, 2026 at 09:35. 6 killed (including 2 teenagers aged 16-17), 36 wounded. 10+ buildings destroyed. Town declared 3-day mourning.

label: Rivne Oblast Residential Hit (May 13)
sub: Russian drone struck a residential building in Rivne Oblast on May 13, 2026 — killing 3 people and injuring 4 others. Part of Russia's 200+ Shahed drone mass attack across 14 Ukrainian regions, the second consecutive large-scale barrage following the May 9–11 ceasefire collapse.

label: Kryvyi Rih Drone Strike (May 13)
sub: Russian drone strike in Kryvyi Rih on May 13, 2026 killed 2 people and wounded 4 others. One of the deadliest individual impact points in Russia's 200+ drone mass attack. City has been repeatedly targeted as Ukraine's fourth-largest urban center.

label: Ryazan Refinery Strike (May 15)
sub: Ukrainian drone forces struck the Rosneft-owned Ryazan oil refinery on May 15, 2026 — Russia's 3rd-largest petroleum facility (17M tonne/year). Vacuum distillation units caught fire; 3 killed, 12 injured. Third Ukrainian attack on this facility in 2026. Commander Brovdi confirmed part of broader 23-target overnight operation.

label: Kryvyi Rih Missile Strike (May 16)
sub: Russian missile hit an industrial infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on May 16, 2026. Explosions reported in city; no immediate mass casualties confirmed. Kryvyi Rih is Ukraine's largest city by area, a major steel/mining center, and President Zelensky's birthplace — a repeated Russian target throughout the war.

label: Be-200 Aircraft Destroyed — Krasnodar Krai
sub: Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Forces destroyed a Beriev Be-200 amphibious aircraft in Krasnodar Krai on May 15–16, 2026 — approximately 1,000 km from the front. Zelensky released footage on May 16 confirming the strike alongside destruction of a Ka-27 helicopter, ammunition transport ship, Pantsir-S1 air defense system, Tor missile system, and Redut-2US communications relay. Described by Zelensky as a 'justified response' to Russia's record May 13–14 aerial assault.

label: Belgorod Region Drone Strike (May 16)
sub: A Ukrainian drone struck a vehicle in Krasnaya Yaruga town, Belgorod Oblast on May 16, 2026, killing 1 male civilian. Belgorod Oblast serves as a Russian staging area for attacks on Kharkiv Oblast and has been the site of ongoing Ukrainian cross-border drone operations throughout the war.

label: Dnipro — Russian Drone Hits 24-Storey Building (May 18)
sub: On May 18, 2026, a Russian Shahed drone struck a 24-storey residential building in Dnipro between 02:00–03:00 local time, injuring 18 people including 2 children (8 hospitalized). Part of Russia's overnight barrage of 524 Shaheds and 22 missiles; 503 drones were intercepted by Ukrainian air defenses. Confirmed by Dnipropetrovsk Governor Oleksandr Hanzha.

label: Black Sea — Russian Drone Hits Chinese Ship KSL Deyang (May 18)
sub: On May 18, 2026, a Russian Shahed drone struck the KSL Deyang — a Chinese-owned cargo vessel (Marshall Islands flag, all-Chinese crew) — as it approached Pivdennyi port to load iron ore concentrate. No casualties; hull partially charred; vessel continued to destination. Incident occurred one day before Putin's scheduled Beijing visit to Xi Jinping. Zelensky: 'Russians could not have been unaware.' Russia did not comment. Confirmed by Al Jazeera.

label: Stepnohirsk — Ukraine Claims Full Control (May 18)
sub: On May 18, 2026, Ukrainian Military Intelligence claimed full control of Stepnohirsk in Zaporizhzhia Oblast — a tactically significant claim amid continued Russian pressure toward the provincial capital of Zaporizhzhia city. The Huliaipole direction in Zaporizhzhia has been one of the most contested sectors throughout May 2026.

label: Izmail Warehouse Strike (May 19)
sub: On May 19, 2026, a Russian Shahed drone struck a warehouse in Izmail district, Odesa Oblast, during Russia's overnight barrage of 209 drones (180 intercepted). Izmail is a major port city on the Danube River near the Romanian border. The strike is part of Russia's continued targeting of Odesa Oblast logistics and infrastructure.

label: Ka-27 Helicopter Destroyed (Black Sea, May 19)
sub: On May 19, 2026, Ukraine's Navy reported the destruction of a Russian Ka-27 military helicopter over the Black Sea. The Ka-27 is a ship-based helicopter used for anti-submarine warfare, search and rescue, and naval operations. The destruction continues Ukraine's campaign to degrade Russian naval aviation assets in the Black Sea theater.

label: Russia Captures Petropavlivka — Kupiansk Direction (May 19)
sub: On May 19, 2026, Russian forces captured Petropavlivka and Stepova Novoselivka in the Kupiansk direction (Kharkiv Oblast), extending Russian pressure east of Kupiansk. The Kupiansk direction has been an active offensive axis for Russian forces throughout 2025-2026, threatening the city of Kupiansk itself.

label: Snizhne — Op. 'Snow for Akhmat' (May 22)
sub: On the night of May 20–21, 2026 (confirmed May 22), Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck the Sever-Akhmat drone pilot training complex in Snizhne, Russian-occupied Donetsk Oblast. Eleven drones armed with 100 kg warheads destroyed a 2,484 sq-meter facility; 65 Chechen (Akhmat) cadets and their commanding officer were killed. Simultaneous strikes hit an FSB headquarters and air defense system — combined ~100 Russian personnel killed/wounded (Zelensky confirmed). Operation 'Snow for Akhmat' highlights Ukraine's precision drone capability targeting Russian military training infrastructure deep in occupied territory.

label: Taganrog Airfield — Tu-142 × 2 + Iskander Destroyed (May 30)
sub: Ukraine's 1st Separate Unmanned Systems Center destroyed two Tu-142 long-range maritime patrol/anti-submarine aircraft and an Iskander-M tactical ballistic missile system at Taganrog military airfield, Rostov Oblast, on the night of May 29–30, 2026. Confirmed by Maj. Brovdi with video evidence. The Tu-142 has no active production line — each loss is irreplaceable for Russian Naval Aviation's Black Sea surveillance. Third major Ukrainian strike on Taganrog area in 2026.

label: Armavir Oil Depot (UA Strike, May 30)
sub: Ukrainian long-range drones struck an oil depot in Armavir, Krasnodar Krai (~500 km from Ukraine's border) on the night of May 29–30, 2026, setting it ablaze. Zelensky confirmed the strike. Part of Ukraine's ongoing 2026 deep-strike energy campaign targeting Russian oil storage and export infrastructure spanning Krasnodar Krai, Volgograd, Moscow, Ryazan, Leningrad and Yaroslavl oblasts.

label: Shostka Railway Station (Destroyed, May 30)
sub: A Russian drone destroyed the railway station building in Shostka, Sumy Oblast on May 30, 2026 and damaged surrounding railway infrastructure. Shostka is approximately 40 km from the Russian border and has been repeatedly struck by Russian cross-border drone attacks throughout the war. The strike continues Russia's systematic campaign to degrade Ukraine's rail logistics network.

label: Novocherkassk Power Plant (Struck Jun 5)
sub: Ukrainian drones struck the Novocherkassk Thermal Power Plant (2,112 MW) in Rostov Oblast on June 5, 2026, causing a regional power outage. Part of Ukraine's sustained 2026 campaign targeting Russian energy generation infrastructure.

label: Odesa (Energy Grid Strike, Jun 5)
sub: Russian forces struck energy infrastructure in Odesa Oblast on June 5, 2026, leaving 33,500 consumers without electricity. Continued Russian campaign against Ukraine's southern power grid.

label: Pokrovsk (Active Front)
sub: Pokrovsk under heaviest Russian frontline pressure as of June 6–7, 2026: 26 Russian attacks in single day; 42 Russian soldiers reported eliminated in this sector alone. Critical logistics hub for Ukrainian forces in central Donetsk Oblast. ISW confirmed recent Russian advances in Pokrovsk direction.

label: Kronstadt Naval Base (2nd Strike, Jun 6)
sub: Ukraine struck Kronstadt naval base and oil complex for the second time in one week on June 6, 2026 — first strike June 3 (SPIEF opening), second strike June 6 (SPIEF closing). Russia claimed 376 drones intercepted overnight across 16 regions, including 86 in Leningrad region. Largest claimed single Ukrainian drone operation of the war.

label: Nizhnekamsk Refinery
sub: Tatarstan oil refinery struck by Ukrainian drones; 13 killed, 39 injured (Aug 10, 2026)

label: Zaporizhzhia
sub: North Korean KN-23 missiles and Zircon strikes kill 6, injure 19+ (Aug 11, 2026)

label: Voronezh
sub: Wildberries logistics hub and Orenburg refinery struck by Ukrainian drones; 1 killed (Aug 11, 2026)

label: Novorossiysk Naval Base
sub: 15-weapon Ukrainian strike damaged 4 Russian warships and 2 grain terminals (Aug 12, 2026)

label: Odesa Port
sub: Iskander-M, Kh-31P, Kh-35 missiles and 138 drones struck fuel depot, tanker, cargo ship (Aug 12, 2026)

label: Berezivka Rail Line
sub: Jet-powered Shahed drone struck Odesa–Dnipro passenger train locomotive, killing driver and assistant (Aug 13, 2026)

label: Salavat Refinery
sub: Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refinery struck by Ukrainian drones — 2nd hit in a month (Aug 13, 2026)

label: Buryn (Sumy Oblast)
sub: Russian jet-powered drones killed a mother and her 9-year-old son in a double-strike attack on a private home (Aug 14, 2026)

label: Kramatorsk / Bilenke
sub: Eight Russian guided aerial bombs struck an apartment block and nearby Bilenke village; 1 killed, 15-18 injured (Aug 14, 2026)

label: Ust-Luga Port
sub: 54-drone Ukrainian strike damaged two processing plants at Russia's Baltic oil terminal — 6th strike on this port in 2026 (Aug 14, 2026)

label: Savasleyka Airbase
sub: Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missiles struck the MiG-31K Kinzhal-carrier airbase in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, ~700km from the border (Aug 15, 2026)

label: Progress Rocket & Space Center (Samara)
sub: Ukraine's Flamingo missiles struck the Roscosmos Progress Rocket and Space Center, ~900km from the border — confirmed by Zelensky (Aug 15, 2026)

label: Zaporizhzhia (Gardening Community)
sub: Russian drone strikes killed a 43-year-old man and 41-year-old woman at a gardening community; separate strike hit a bread delivery vehicle near Bilenke (Aug 17, 2026)

label: Koloskovo (Belgorod Region)
sub: Ukrainian rocket strike killed 6 and wounded 4 in Koloskovo village, ~24km from the Ukraine border (Aug 17, 2026)

label: Pechenihy (Kharkiv Region)
sub: Russian Banderol missiles killed 10 and wounded 18+ at a residential intersection; nearby Izyum also hit, wounding 5 (Aug 18, 2026)

label: Moscow Region
sub: Ukraine launched 620+ drones at Moscow Oblast, hitting a Wildberries warehouse, Pavlovsky Posad, and other facilities — largest drone attack on Moscow in 2 years per TASS (Aug 18, 2026)

label: Kherson (Bus Strike)
sub: Russian drone strike on a bus killed 4 and wounded 4 in Kherson city; a separate strike killed 1 more (Aug 19, 2026)

label: Dzerzhinsk (Sverdlov Explosives Plant)
sub: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Sverdlov explosives plant, sparking a large fire (Aug 19, 2026)

label: Kyiv (Massive Barrage)
sub: Russia launched an hours-long ballistic/cruise missile and drone barrage on Kyiv, killing 15+ (Aug 20, 2026)

label: Kryvyi Rih (Shopping Mall)
sub: Russian double-tap drone strike on the Solnechnaya Galereya mall killed 16+ and injured 130+ (Aug 21, 2026)

label: Tokarivka (Mykolaiv Region)
sub: Russian Shahed strike killed 4, including 3 children, at a village store/post office (Aug 21, 2026)

label: Kyiv (Darnytskyi District)
sub: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv's Darnytskyi district, killing 1 (Aug 22, 2026)

label: Chapaevsk (Ozon Warehouse)
sub: Ukrainian drones struck the Ozon logistics complex and Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery in Samara region for the first time (Aug 22, 2026)

label: Izium (Kharkiv Region)
sub: Russian guided bombs damaged ~20 houses; 2–4 injured (Aug 23, 2026)

label: Kharkiv (Osnovianskyi District)
sub: Jet-powered Russian drone struck a residential area, injuring 8 (Aug 23, 2026)

label: Orenburg (Ozon Warehouse)
sub: Ukrainian drones reportedly struck an Ozon logistics center ~1,000km from the border (Aug 23, 2026)

label: Kharkiv Oblast (Independence Day Barrage)
sub: Nationwide Independence Day barrage killed 5, injured 17 in Kharkiv Oblast; 8 killed, 43 injured nationwide (Aug 24, 2026)

label: Chernihiv (Residential Building)
sub: Russian Geran-5 drone struck a 9-story residential building at midday, injuring 20 (Aug 24, 2026)

label: Kamensk-Shakhtinsky (Kombinat Kamenskiy)
sub: Ukrainian drones struck the Kombinat Kamenskiy rocket-fuel plant as part of a 66-target overnight strike (Aug 24, 2026)

label: Kyiv (Nationwide Barrage)
sub: Russian barrage on 9 cities hit four Kyiv districts — residential blocks, a school, a medical facility (Aug 27, 2026)

label: Zaporizhzhia
sub: Russian strike killed a 78-year-old woman and injured 7, including 3 children (Aug 27, 2026)

label: Kharkiv (Epicentr Mall)
sub: Russian jet-powered drone killed 1, injured 5 at a shopping mall (Aug 27, 2026)

label: Occupied Donetsk (Command Posts)
sub: Ukrainian cruise missiles struck Russian army command post facilities (Aug 26–27, 2026)
